applies_why: The judge is resolving a link collision (D5 vs C5) where the defender's chain [CR2] G is set against the challenger's rows, so K-C governs how that collision is weighed.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] G answers the 'almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows, leaving the sign's sense open.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: leaving the sign's sense open — (1) a finding of ambiguity after chain weighing, allowed; (2) a demand for an explicit stating verse, forbidden. I read it as (1).
why: The judge does not require any single verse to state the contrary; it finds the sign's sense open after the defender's chain answers the challenger's rows, which is a chain-level underdetermination rather than a verse-by-verse stating-verse test.
